metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable entry point is present (src/PAYRUN.cbl PROCEDURE DIVISION / MAIN-PARA, invoked as PGM=PAYRUN by jcl/PAYRUN.jcl) with no multiple service units, no library packaging manifest, and no resource-provisioning IaC. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: No message-queue consumers and no multi-service orchestration; the program owns persistent state (indexed EMPMAST dataset plus DB2 per README) and performs writes (PAY-FILE output, FTP push) with real calculation logic rather than read-only paginated queries.

tech_stack.framework: None — z/OS batch (CA-7 scheduled), IBM DB2 for z/OS v10
tech_stack.architecture: Mainframe batch monolith with nightly plain-FTP file exchange to an EC2 file gateway

metadata.counts_note: All 43 rubric questions accounted for: 40 findings + 3 evaluations.

findings.title: Documented API Interface
findings.description: The system exposes no REST, GraphQL, gRPC or AsyncAPI interface. The only integration surfaces are (a) direct VSAM/DB2 dataset access (`SELECT EMP-FILE ASSIGN TO EMPMAST`, `src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 13-17) and (b) nightly plain-FTP transfer of a fixed-width flat file to an EC2 gateway (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 14-21). README confirms: 'Integration: Nightly FTP of fixed-width files to/from EC2 gateway'. Searched for Express/Flask/Spring/gin route patterns, OpenAPI/Swagger/GraphQL/Smithy files and RPA scripts across all 4 repository files — zero results.
findings.gap: No callable, documented programmatic interface exists for an agent to bind a tool to. Integration today requires dataset-level access or file drops, which are non-auditable, batch-latency-bound, and brittle.
findings.recommendation: Expose payroll read and calculation operations through an API facade (z/OS Connect EE, or an API Gateway + Lambda service in front of the EC2 gateway) with an OpenAPI contract, before attempting any agent integration.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Expose payroll read and calculation operations through an API facade (z/OS Connect EE, or an API Gateway + Lambda service in front of the EC2 gateway) with an OpenAPI contract, before attempting any agent integration.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Expose payroll read and calculation operations through an API facade (z/OS Connect EE, or an API Gateway + Lambda service in front of the EC2 gateway) with an OpenAPI contract, before attempting any agent integration.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: No idempotency mechanism exists. `PROCESS-EMP` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 44-56) unconditionally recomputes and `WRITE`s a pay record per employee, and the JCL allocates a new GDG generation each execution (`PAYOUT DD DSN=ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT(+1),DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE)`). There is no run key, no idempotency token, no duplicate-run detection, and `STEP020` re-FTPs `ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT` unconditionally.
findings.gap: A retried or duplicated invocation produces a second payout file and a second plaintext FTP push, with no business key preventing duplicate payment for the same pay period.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a pay-period run key (period id + sequence) persisted and checked before processing, and make the FTP/publish step conditional on that key so re-execution is a no-op rather than a duplicate payout.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and no idempotency key or duplicate-run guard exists on the payout write path.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true (the program writes PAYOUT and FTPs it), so API-Q4 resolves at its write-enabled severity. A retried agent invocation would duplicate payroll disbursement records.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Introduce a pay-period run key (period id + sequence) persisted and checked before processing, and make the FTP/publish step conditional on that key so re-execution is a no-op rather than a duplicate payout.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Introduce a pay-period run key (period id + sequence) persisted and checked before processing, and make the FTP/publish step conditional on that key so re-execution is a no-op rather than a duplicate payout.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: No machine identity mechanism of any kind. The only authentication artifact in the repository is a shared static FTP userid and password embedded in JCL: `payroll PayR0ll2003!` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 18). Job identity is the submitting human user (`NOTIFY=&SYSUID`). Searched for OAuth2 client-credentials, mTLS, API keys with principal attribution, Cognito app clients and API Gateway authorizers — none present.
findings.gap: There is no way to issue a distinct machine/agent principal, and no principal attribution available to downstream authorization or audit. Every invocation looks like the same shared `payroll` account or the submitting RACF user.
findings.recommendation: Provision a distinct machine identity per agent (IAM role or OAuth2 client-credentials client at the API facade, RACF/ACF2 surrogate id on the mainframe side) and carry the principal through to DB2/dataset access.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Provision a distinct machine identity per agent (IAM role or OAuth2 client-credentials client at the API facade, RACF/ACF2 surrogate id on the mainframe side) and carry the principal through to DB2/dataset access.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Provision a distinct machine identity per agent (IAM role or OAuth2 client-credentials client at the API facade, RACF/ACF2 surrogate id on the mainframe side) and carry the principal through to DB2/dataset access.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of the authenticated principal for write operations. The program emits only `SYSOUT DD SYSOUT=*` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 13) — unstructured spool output with no principal field. There is no CloudTrail, no S3 Object Lock, no log retention or tamper-evidence configuration anywhere in the repository (no IaC files exist at all).
findings.gap: Payroll disbursement writes (PAYOUT generation and FTP push) produce no immutable, attributable audit record. Agent-initiated actions could not be distinguished from human-initiated runs, nor proven for SOX purposes.
findings.recommendation: Emit a structured per-run audit record (principal, run key, record count, totals, timestamp) to an append-only store (SMF offload or S3 with Object Lock) and attribute it to the machine identity from AUTH-Q1.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and no immutable, principal-attributed audit trail exists for the payout write path.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true, so AUTH-Q6 resolves at its write-enabled severity rather than the read-only RISK-SAFETY severity. Payroll is SOX-relevant, making an unattributable write trail a compliance exposure.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Emit a structured per-run audit record (principal, run key, record count, totals, timestamp) to an append-only store (SMF offload or S3 with Object Lock) and attribute it to the machine identity from AUTH-Q1.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Emit a structured per-run audit record (principal, run key, record count, totals, timestamp) to an append-only store (SMF offload or S3 with Object Lock) and attribute it to the machine identity from AUTH-Q1.

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: No compensation or rollback. `MAIN-PARA` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 36-43) opens the files, loops to EOF and `STOP RUN`s; there is no file-status checking, no checkpoint/restart, no undo of records already written, and no coordination between `STEP010` (compute/write) and `STEP020` (FTP push) in `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl`. An abend after partial processing leaves a partial PAYOUT generation catalogued, and a failure after FTP leaves the gateway holding a partial file.
findings.gap: The two-step write sequence (compute+write, then transmit) has no compensating action. Partial state is neither detected nor reversible.
findings.recommendation: Add checkpoint/restart (or a staging dataset promoted only on clean completion), explicit FILE STATUS handling in the COBOL, and make STEP020 conditional (`COND`/`IF`) on STEP010 completion so a failed run cannot publish partial payroll.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the multi-step write sequence has no rollback or compensating transaction.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true and the job is a genuine multi-step write workflow (compute/write then transmit), so STATE-Q1 resolves at its write-enabled severity.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add checkpoint/restart (or a staging dataset promoted only on clean completion), explicit FILE STATUS handling in the COBOL, and make STEP020 conditional (`COND`/`IF`) on STEP010 completion so a failed run cannot publish partial payroll.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Add checkpoint/restart (or a staging dataset promoted only on clean completion), explicit FILE STATUS handling in the COBOL, and make STEP020 conditional (`COND`/`IF`) on STEP010 completion so a failed run cannot publish partial payroll.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A = Yes: the employee master record holds `EMP-SSN PIC 9(09)` and `EMP-ACCT PIC X(17)` (bank account) alongside name, rate and hours (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 21-27), and README lists 'Plaintext FTP of SSN and bank account data' as a known issue. Stage B1 fires: there is no field scoping of any kind — `STEP020` transmits the whole `ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT` dataset over plain FTP, and any consumer reading `EMPMAST` receives the full record including SSN and account number. Stage B2 fires: access is dataset-level with `DISP=SHR` and a single shared `payroll` credential — no differentiation between sensitive and non-sensitive access. Stage B3: no classification tags, field annotations, or Macie-equivalent tooling exist.
findings.gap: Sensitive fields (SSN, bank account) are not excluded from, or separately authorized within, the data a consumer or agent would retrieve. One credential grants everything.
findings.recommendation: Define a scoped projection for agent consumption that omits SSN and account number (separate, separately-authorized endpoint for the disbursement path only), and add field-level classification annotations to the record layout and its API representation.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: Stage A=Yes (SSN and bank account persisted), B1 fires under agent_scope=write-enabled because no response/field scoping exists.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_persistent_data_store=true with PII and financial instruments in EMP-RECORD; no serialization exclusion, projection, or separately-scoped access path exists, so B1 fires at its write-enabled BLOCKER severity.

b1.reasoning: No field exclusion or projection: EMPMAST consumers and the FTP push both carry EMP-SSN and EMP-ACCT in full (src/PAYRUN.cbl lines 25-26, jcl/PAYRUN.jcl lines 14-21).

b2.reasoning: Access is dataset-level via DISP=SHR plus one shared 'payroll' FTP credential; no scope, role, or column-level differentiation between sensitive and non-sensitive data.

b3.reasoning: No classification tags, field-level sensitivity annotations, data catalog entries, or PII detection tooling present in any of the 4 repository files.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Define a scoped projection for agent consumption that omits SSN and account number (separate, separately-authorized endpoint for the disbursement path only), and add field-level classification annotations to the record layout and its API representation.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Define a scoped projection for agent consumption that omits SSN and account number (separate, separately-authorized endpoint for the disbursement path only), and add field-level classification annotations to the record layout and its API representation.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: Payroll data containing SSN and bank account numbers is transmitted unencrypted across a trust boundary to an EC2-hosted gateway at a hardcoded private IP (`open 10.0.7.40`, `ascii`, `put 'ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT' /incoming/payout.dat`, `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 14-21). No residency, sovereignty, region-pinning or cross-region replication control appears anywhere in the repository, and no GDPR/LGPD/jurisdictional statement exists in `README.md` — the only compliance-adjacent note is that the plaintext FTP of SSN and bank data is a known issue.
findings.gap: There is no declared or enforced boundary for where this regulated payroll data may travel, and no encryption in transit on the one hop that does cross a boundary. Nothing would prevent an agent from relaying the data to an out-of-jurisdiction endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Classify the payroll dataset's residency constraints explicitly, replace plain FTP with an encrypted, region-pinned transfer (SFTP/TLS to an in-region endpoint), and record the permitted-destination policy as enforceable configuration.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled, has_persistent_data_store=true, and no residency control or in-transit protection exists on the cross-boundary hop.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The surface-flag downgrade does not apply (has_persistent_data_store=true), so DATA-Q2 resolves at its write-enabled BLOCKER severity. Regulated payroll PII leaves the mainframe boundary in cleartext with no declared jurisdiction policy.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Classify the payroll dataset's residency constraints explicitly, replace plain FTP with an encrypted, region-pinned transfer (SFTP/TLS to an in-region endpoint), and record the permitted-destination policy as enforceable configuration.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Classify the payroll dataset's residency constraints explicitly, replace plain FTP with an encrypted, region-pinned transfer (SFTP/TLS to an in-region endpoint), and record the permitted-destination policy as enforceable configuration.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: Authorization is entirely coarse-grained. The job runs with `REGION=0M` (unbounded storage) under the submitter's identity, datasets are shared with `DISP=SHR` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 1-7), and the one credential present (`payroll`) is a single shared account used for the whole transfer. No IAM policies, RACF profile definitions, scopes, or any other mechanism for differentiating access levels exist in the repository.
findings.gap: There is no mechanism to grant a caller read-only access to a subset of payroll data. Any identity that can run or read this job inherits the full surface.
findings.recommendation: Define scoped profiles per capability (read-employee-summary vs. generate-payout vs. transmit) as RACF dataset profiles and, at the future API facade, IAM/OAuth scopes bound to the machine identity.

compensating_controls: Restrict the batch surface to a single operator-controlled submission path and keep the agent out of the mainframe boundary entirely during pilot.
Front payroll reads with a narrow read-only service account whose RACF profile grants only the summary dataset.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization. There are no permission checks in `src/PAYRUN.cbl` — the program unconditionally opens `EMP-FILE` for input and `PAY-FILE` for output (lines 37-38) with authority derived solely from the batch job's identity. No `canRead`/`canWrite` equivalents, ABAC policies, or method-level authorization exist anywhere (no middleware, no IaC, no API layer).
findings.gap: Read and write authority are inseparable: anything permitted to invoke the payroll calculation is permitted to generate and transmit a payout. An agent restricted to reads cannot be enforced technically.
findings.recommendation: Split the read path from the write path into separately authorized operations at the API facade and bind distinct RACF/IAM permissions to each, so read-only agent scope is enforceable rather than declarative.

compensating_controls: Deploy an agent against a read-only replica/extract so write authority is physically unavailable.
Require an operator to perform the transmit step manually during pilot.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation or delegation. The only identity in the pipeline is `NOTIFY=&SYSUID` (the submitting user, `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 1) for notification purposes and the shared `payroll` FTP account for the transfer hop (line 18). No JWT parsing, token exchange, on-behalf-of flow, or user-context header exists, and the COBOL program receives no caller context at all.
findings.gap: The system cannot distinguish an agent acting as itself from an agent acting on behalf of a specific user, and no caller identity survives the FTP hop to the EC2 gateway — the gateway sees only the shared account.
findings.recommendation: Carry a propagated principal (and, where applicable, an on-behalf-of subject) from the API facade through to the batch invocation and the gateway hop, and record both actor and subject distinctly.

compensating_controls: Restrict pilot agents to agent-as-self identity only; prohibit on-behalf-of payroll workflows until propagation exists.
Record the requesting human in the invocation payload and reconcile it against the operator log out of band.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: A production credential is hardcoded in version-controlled source: `payroll PayR0ll2003!` in the inline FTP input of `STEP020` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 18). The JCL comment states 'DATASET NAMES AND DB2 CREDS HARDCODED - SEE OPS RUNBOOK' (line 4) and README lists 'Hardcoded dataset names and credentials in JCL' as a known issue. No Secrets Manager, Vault, or any secrets-management reference exists; the password's embedded year suggests it has not rotated since 2003.
findings.gap: A long-lived plaintext credential for the payroll transfer account is readable by anyone with repository access and is present in git history. No rotation mechanism exists.
findings.recommendation: Rotate the `payroll` account credential immediately, move it to AWS Secrets Manager (or the mainframe equivalent) with scheduled rotation, and retrieve it at run time rather than embedding it in JCL. Treat the current value as compromised and purge it from history.

compensating_controls: Rotate the credential immediately and restrict repository access while the secrets-manager migration is in flight.
Network-restrict the gateway so the credential is only usable from the mainframe source address.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: No per-identity suspension or revocation capability. There is a single shared FTP account (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 18) and no API keys, service accounts, IAM roles, or user-pool entries that could be individually disabled. Revoking access would mean disabling the one shared `payroll` account, which stops the entire payroll pipeline.
findings.gap: A misbehaving agent identity cannot be isolated without taking down payroll processing for everyone — there is no per-identity kill switch.
findings.recommendation: Issue one revocable credential/role per consuming identity and verify that disabling an individual identity leaves the batch pipeline and other consumers operational.

compensating_controls: Keep a documented, tested procedure to disable the API facade's agent credential independently of the batch pipeline.
Gate agent access behind a feature flag that can be switched off without touching the shared account.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No concurrency control. `EMP-FILE` is opened `ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL` with `DISP=SHR` on `ACME.PAYROLL.EMPMAST` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 13-17, `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 7) — shared disposition with no enqueue, no record-level locking, no version field in `EMP-RECORD`, and no optimistic-concurrency token. Nothing prevents two concurrent PAYRUN executions, and both would write to their own new GDG generation from the same mutable master.
findings.gap: Concurrent invocations can read the employee master mid-update and produce divergent or duplicated payout files; there is no conflict detection to reject the second writer.
findings.recommendation: Add a run-level enqueue (dataset ENQ or a scheduler mutex) so only one payroll calculation can execute per period, and add a version/last-updated column to the employee master for optimistic concurrency at the record level.

compensating_controls: Enforce single-run-at-a-time via the CA-7 schedule and prohibit ad-hoc concurrent submission during pilot.
Serialize all agent-initiated invocations through a single-threaded queue.

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: No resilience controls on external dependencies. `READ-EMP` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 57-59) handles only `AT END` — there is no `FILE STATUS` clause, no I/O error branch, and no `INVALID KEY` handling. The FTP step (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 15-21) runs a fixed inline script with no timeout, no retry, no return-code check and no failure path if `10.0.7.40` is unreachable. README notes DB2 v10 is out of support and the batch window overruns at 5-7 hours.
findings.gap: A slow or unavailable dependency (DB2, the EC2 gateway) produces an abend or a silent partial result rather than a bounded, retried, circuit-broken failure — and an agent calling in would observe no distinction.
findings.recommendation: Add FILE STATUS and I/O error handling to the COBOL, bounded retries with backoff and a return-code gate on the transfer step, and a timeout/circuit-breaker at the API facade that fails fast instead of queueing behind a 5-7 hour batch.

compensating_controls: Put a timeout and fail-fast wrapper at the API facade so agents never block on the batch window or an unreachable gateway.
Alert on batch duration and gateway reachability so degradation is detected before agents cascade.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No blast-radius or transaction limits. `PERFORM PROCESS-EMP UNTIL WS-EOF = 'Y'` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 41) processes the entire employee master unconditionally — there is no maximum-records cap, no total-disbursement ceiling, no per-caller batch-size limit, and no spend threshold. `SPACE=(CYL,(50,10),RLSE)` is a storage allocation, not a business limit.
findings.gap: A single invocation can generate payout records for every employee with no cap on record count or total monetary value, so an erroneous agent-initiated run has unbounded financial blast radius.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable per-run business limits (max employees processed, max aggregate net disbursement, max variance vs. prior period) that abort the run and require explicit human override when exceeded.

compensating_controls: Apply limits in the agent orchestration layer (max records per request, mandatory human sign-off above a monetary threshold) until system-side limits exist.
Restrict pilot scope to read and report operations with no disbursement authority.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No draft or pending state. `PROCESS-EMP` writes final pay records directly (`WRITE PAY-RECORD`, `src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 55) and the output generation is immediately catalogued (`DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE)`) and FTP'd to the gateway in the next step. `PAY-RECORD` is an opaque `PIC X(120)` with no status field, and there is no PENDING/DRAFT/PROPOSED state or create-then-confirm sequence anywhere.
findings.gap: There is no reviewable intermediate state between calculation and disbursement, so a proposed payroll run cannot be inspected and approved before it is committed and transmitted.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a proposed-run state: write to a staging dataset with an explicit status, and promote/transmit only on an approval action. This also provides the review point HITL-Q2 needs.

compensating_controls: Have the agent write only to a separate proposal dataset that an operator promotes manually.
Keep the agent advisory-only (produces a recommendation document, not a payout) during pilot.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No configurable approval gate. The pipeline is a fully automated CA-7 schedule — `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 3 states 'RUNS EVERY OTHER FRIDAY VIA CA-7 SCHEDULE PAYRUN-BW' and `STEP020` transmits immediately after `STEP010` with no intervening confirmation step, approval endpoint, or operation-level flag. No approval API, no waitForTaskToken-equivalent, no manual hold is defined.
findings.gap: High-impact operations (generating and transmitting a payroll disbursement file) cannot be configured to require human approval at the system layer; the only control is the scheduler.
findings.recommendation: Add an operation-level approval flag that holds the transmit step pending explicit human release, configurable per operation type (e.g., always required for off-cycle runs or runs exceeding the STATE-Q6 limits).

compensating_controls: Enforce approval in the orchestration layer before invoking the job, and keep CA-7 as the sole production trigger.
Require dual operator sign-off on every off-cycle run.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: No PII redaction in observable output. The job writes diagnostics to `SYSOUT DD SYSOUT=*` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 13) — unfiltered JES spool with no scrubbing layer. The processed records contain `EMP-SSN` and `EMP-ACCT` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 25-26), and any abend dump or diagnostic trace of the record area would expose them verbatim. No log-scrubbing middleware, masking utility, CloudWatch filter, or Macie-equivalent exists in the repository.
findings.gap: Employee SSNs and bank account numbers sit in the working record area with no masking policy, so abend dumps and spool output are an uncontrolled PII egress path.
findings.recommendation: Mask SSN and account fields in any diagnostic output, route spool to a retention-bounded, access-controlled destination, and add a redaction filter before logs reach any downstream observability system.

compensating_controls: Restrict spool and dump access to the payroll operations group and set short retention while redaction is implemented.
Prohibit forwarding of JES spool into any shared observability platform until a redaction filter exists.

findings.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
findings.description: No asynchronous invocation pattern, despite operations far exceeding any synchronous budget: README states the batch 'runs 5-7 hours and sometimes overruns'. Execution is a scheduled CA-7 job (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 3) with no job-submission API, no status/polling endpoint, and no webhook callback. Completion is signalled only by `NOTIFY=&SYSUID` (line 1) and the appearance of a new GDG generation.
findings.gap: An agent has no way to submit work, obtain a job handle, poll status, or receive a completion callback for a multi-hour operation.
findings.recommendation: Expose a submit/poll/callback trio at the API facade (job id on submit, status endpoint, optional webhook on completion) wrapping the CA-7 job, so agents never hold a synchronous connection against the batch window.

compensating_controls: Have the orchestration layer treat payroll operations as fire-and-check-later with its own job tracking.
Limit pilot agents to reading completed prior-period outputs rather than triggering runs.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: Current state is not queryable. `EMP-FILE` is read `ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL` from end to end (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 13-17) even though the dataset is INDEXED, and the output is an opaque fixed-width `PAY-RECORD PIC X(120)` (line 29). There is no status field, no state machine, and no query interface — inspecting current payroll state requires reading a flat file or the DB2 tables directly.
findings.gap: An agent cannot inspect employee or pay-run state before acting; it would have to parse a 120-byte fixed-width file or obtain direct database access.
findings.recommendation: Expose read endpoints for employee and pay-run state (including run status and per-period totals) so an agent can read before acting instead of parsing batch output.

compensating_controls: Publish a periodic state extract the agent can read instead of querying live state.
Have the orchestration layer cache last-known run status from operator notifications.

findings.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
findings.description: No degradation signalling. The program's only state variable for control flow is `WS-EOF` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 35); there is no health surface, no freshness or staleness indicator, and no partial-result marker. Critically, README documents that the state tax table lookup 'REMOVED IN 2011, DONE MANUALLY' (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 50) and tax tables are 'updated by hand each January' — the system is permanently running in a functionally degraded mode that it does not advertise.
findings.gap: Consumers receive net-pay figures that silently omit state tax and may be based on stale hand-maintained tax tables, with no machine-readable signal that the result is partial.
findings.recommendation: Emit an explicit completeness/freshness indicator with every result (e.g., tax-table effective date, `state_tax_applied: false`) so an agent can detect degraded output and defer to human review.

compensating_controls: Document the known-incomplete calculation (no state tax, manual tax tables) in the agent's tool description so it never presents net pay as authoritative.
Require human review of any agent output derived from net-pay figures.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: There is no environment definition in the repository — no docker-compose, no environment-specific configuration, no seed or synthetic data generator, and no IaC. Dataset names are hardcoded to production-looking qualifiers (`ACME.PAYROLL.EMPMAST`, `ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT`) in `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 6-8, and README states changes are 'validated in a shared QA region only' with 'No automated tests'.
findings.gap: A shared QA region with no committed configuration and no production-shaped synthetic data is not a safe, reproducible place to exercise agent behaviour, and promotion requires hand-editing hardcoded dataset names.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize dataset qualifiers by environment (symbolic parameters), and stand up an isolated sandbox region seeded with synthetic employee data that matches the production record layout.

compensating_controls: Exercise agent behaviour against a frozen copy of a prior-period output file rather than the QA region.
Schedule agent testing in the QA region in exclusive windows to avoid shared-region interference.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation. `PROCESS-EMP` computes directly from the input record (`COMPUTE WS-GROSS = EMP-RATE * EMP-HOURS`, `src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 45-47) with no range, sanity, or completeness checks, and `READ-EMP` (lines 57-59) has no `FILE STATUS` or `INVALID KEY` handling. The `PIC` clauses provide implicit truncation only — `WS-GROSS PIC 9(07)V99` will silently truncate an overflowing product rather than reject it, and there is no structured rejection path or error record. No validation library or request validator exists (no API layer at all).
findings.gap: Malformed or out-of-range input (negative/absurd hours, corrupt packed fields, truncated records) is silently computed into a payout rather than rejected with a field-level error.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit field validation with an ON SIZE ERROR branch and a reject-record path that identifies the failing employee id and field, and enforce schema validation at the future API boundary.

compensating_controls: Validate payloads at the orchestration layer before invoking the job.
Reconcile run totals against the prior period and halt on variance beyond a threshold.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: No temporal metadata. `EMP-RECORD` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 20-27) has no created/updated/effective-date field, and `PAY-RECORD` carries only employee id, name and net pay via the `STRING` concatenation (lines 51-55) — no pay-period date, no run timestamp, no timezone normalization. Freshness is implicit in the GDG generation number. The FICA wage base is a hardcoded literal (`WS-WAGE-BASE ... VALUE 132900.00`, line 34) last updated in 2019 per the file header, with no effective-date field.
findings.gap: An agent cannot determine which pay period a record belongs to, when the underlying data was last updated, or whether the embedded tax constants are current.
findings.recommendation: Add pay-period and last-updated timestamps (UTC) to the record layouts and the output file, and externalize the wage base and tax tables with explicit effective dates.

compensating_controls: Have the orchestration layer stamp period and retrieval time onto every extract it reads.
Pin the agent to a single named GDG generation so the period is unambiguous.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning or contract management. The interchange contract is an undocumented fixed-width layout defined only by `DCB=(RECFM=FB,LRECL=120,BLKSIZE=0)` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 12) and the `STRING` statement that builds it (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 51-55); README lists 'Fixed-width file formats with no schema/versioning' as a known issue. There are no copybooks in the repository, no JSON/Avro/Protobuf schema, no migration files, no changelog, and no CI breaking-change detection (no CI configuration exists). The source header warns 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM'.
findings.gap: Consumers reverse-engineer byte offsets from code. Any field addition or width change silently breaks every downstream parser with no version marker or detection gate.
findings.recommendation: Publish the record layout as a versioned, machine-readable schema (copybook plus a generated JSON Schema), add a version marker to the file, and gate changes with automated breaking-change detection in CI.

compensating_controls: Freeze the record layout for the pilot duration and pin the agent's parser to that version.
Maintain a hand-authored copybook in the repository as the interim contract of record.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No tracing and no structured logging. The sole diagnostic output is `SYSOUT DD SYSOUT=*` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 13) — unstructured JES spool. `src/PAYRUN.cbl` contains no DISPLAY statements, no correlation or run id, and no counters. Searched for OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, `traceparent` propagation, JSON logging and `request_id`/`correlation_id` fields across all repository files — zero results.
findings.gap: An agent-initiated run cannot be correlated end-to-end (API facade to batch job to FTP hop), and there is no structured record of what the run did, making failures effectively undiagnosable.
findings.recommendation: Generate a run/correlation id at invocation, carry it through the job and the transfer step, and emit structured (JSON) run events including record counts, totals and outcome to a queryable log store.

compensating_controls: Correlate manually via run id recorded in the orchestration layer plus job number from the notification.
Retain spool for the pilot window so failures can be reconstructed by hand.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: No automated tests exist. The repository contains four files (`.gitignore`, `README.md`, `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl`, `src/PAYRUN.cbl`) — there is no test directory, no unit-test harness, no integration or contract tests, and no CI configuration to run them. README states plainly: 'No automated tests; changes validated in a shared QA region only'. The source header's 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM' warning indicates change confidence rests on tribal knowledge.
findings.gap: Payroll calculation logic (gross, FICA, net) has zero regression coverage, so behaviour changes that would mislead an agent — or miscalculate pay — are caught only by manual QA inspection.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for the calculation paragraphs against fixed input/expected-output fixtures and a file-level golden-output test for the payout layout, and run both in CI on every change.

compensating_controls: Add golden-file regression checks for the pilot-relevant calculation paths only.
Require manual QA sign-off with a documented checklist on every change during pilot.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption at rest for the payroll data stores. There is no IaC in the repository, so no `kms_key_id`, no customer-managed key, and no DB2/dataset encryption setting is declared anywhere. `ACME.PAYROLL.EMPMAST` and the `ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT` generations (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 6-12) are allocated with no encryption attribute, and the transferred file lands on the EC2 gateway at `/incoming/payout.dat` (line 20) with no declared volume encryption. These datasets hold SSN and bank account data.
findings.gap: Payroll PII is stored on mainframe datasets and an EC2 gateway filesystem with no evidence of encryption at rest or key management.
findings.recommendation: Enable dataset encryption (z/OS pervasive encryption with a managed key) on EMPMAST and the PAYOUT GDG, enable EBS/KMS encryption on the gateway volume, and declare both as code so the control is auditable.

compensating_controls: Verify and document existing storage-level encryption out of band; restrict dataset and gateway filesystem access in the interim.
Shorten retention of the payout file on the gateway to the minimum needed.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — the system exposes no callable API surface, so there is no interface for a machine-readable specification to describe. Searched for `openapi.*`, `swagger.*`, `*.graphql`, `*.gql`, `*.smithy` and AsyncAPI files across the repository: none found. The nearest thing to a contract is the implicit 120-byte fixed-width record layout in `src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 51-55.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — machine-readable spec is not applicable until an API facade exists (API-Q1).
findings.recommendation: When the API facade from API-Q1 is built, generate its OpenAPI specification from annotations rather than maintaining it by hand.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there are no API responses to structure. Failure signalling today is an abend plus JES return code; `READ-EMP` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 57-59) has no FILE STATUS clause, so there is no error code, message, or retryable indicator available to any caller.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — structured error responses are not applicable until an API facade exists.
findings.recommendation: Design the API facade's error contract up front with an error code, message and explicit retryable flag, and back it with FILE STATUS handling in the COBOL (see DATA-Q4).

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: The response format is a fixed-width, positional, 120-byte flat file: `PAY-RECORD PIC X(120)` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 29) populated by a `STRING ... DELIMITED BY SIZE` concatenation of employee id, name and net pay (lines 51-55), allocated as `RECFM=FB,LRECL=120` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 12) and transferred in FTP `ascii` mode. There is no JSON, XML, or self-describing binary format.
findings.gap: Positional fixed-width output has no field names, so every consumer (and any agent tool) needs an out-of-band byte-offset map. EBCDIC/ASCII conversion in the FTP step adds a second interpretation hazard for packed numeric fields.
findings.recommendation: Have the API facade emit JSON with named fields, derived from a published copybook, rather than passing the fixed-width layout through to consumers.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission. State changes are visible only as a new catalogued GDG generation and a file landing at `/incoming/payout.dat` on the gateway (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 9-20). There is no webhook, SNS/EventBridge/SQS integration, Kafka topic, or CDC pipeline — the only notification mechanism is `NOTIFY=&SYSUID` (line 1), which targets a human TSO user.
findings.gap: Agents cannot react to payroll state changes; they would have to poll for a new file generation on a biweekly cadence.
findings.recommendation: Publish a completion event (run id, period, record count, status) to EventBridge or SNS when the run finishes, so event-reactive consumers do not need to poll the dataset.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there is no API layer at which to enforce rate limits. Invocation is gated instead by the CA-7 biweekly schedule (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 3), and the job requests unbounded storage with `REGION=0M` (line 1). No API Gateway throttle, WAF rate rule, or rate-limiting middleware exists.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — API-layer rate limiting is not applicable. Scheduler-based invocation incidentally bounds call frequency today, but that protection disappears the moment an API facade is added.
findings.recommendation: Add throttling at the API facade when it is introduced, sized to the batch window, and replace `REGION=0M` with a bounded region to cap a single run's resource consumption.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality measurement. There is no profiling report, null-rate monitor, duplicate detection, freshness SLA, or quality dashboard anywhere in the repository. Known quality hazards are documented but unmeasured: state tax lookup 'REMOVED IN 2011, DONE MANUALLY' (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 50), tax tables 'updated by hand each January' and the FICA wage base hardcoded at the 2019 value (line 34).
findings.gap: An agent reasoning over this payroll data has no completeness signal and would treat manually-patched, structurally incomplete net-pay figures as authoritative.
findings.recommendation: Instrument basic quality metrics for each run (record counts, null/zero-rate on rate and hours, period-over-period variance) and publish them alongside the run, pairing with the degradation signal in STATE-Q7.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Field names are legacy COBOL abbreviations requiring a data dictionary: `EMP-ID`, `EMP-RATE`, `EMP-HOURS`, `EMP-SSN`, `EMP-ACCT` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 21-27) and working-storage names `WS-GROSS`, `WS-FICA`, `WS-FICA-RATE`, `WS-WAGE-BASE`, `WS-NET`, `WS-EOF` (lines 31-35). They are at least domain-recognizable rather than opaque codes, but the output `PAY-RECORD` is wholly positional with no field names at all, and no data dictionary file exists in the repository.
findings.gap: An LLM can infer most of these abbreviations (EMP-ACCT, WS-FICA) from context, so semantic readiness is moderate rather than poor — but the positional output file carries no names whatsoever and the 17-character `EMP-ACCT` has no documented format.
findings.recommendation: Publish a data dictionary mapping each PIC field to a semantic name, type and format, and use expanded names (employeeId, grossPay, ficaWithheld, netPay) in the API facade's JSON representation.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer. The repository has no Glue Catalog reference, no DataHub/Collibra/Alation entry, no metadata files and no schema documentation; `README.md` is a 24-line architecture-and-known-issues summary with no field or dataset inventory. Semantic knowledge of the DB2 tables and the EMPMAST layout lives in the ops runbook referenced from `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 4 and in retired authors' tribal knowledge ('AUTHOR: R. ANDERSON (RETIRED 2014)').
findings.gap: Teams building agent tools against payroll have no discoverable description of what data exists or what it means, which directly slows tool definition and raises the risk of misinterpreting fields.
findings.recommendation: Catalog the payroll datasets and DB2 tables with field-level descriptions and sensitivity labels, starting from the record layouts in `src/PAYRUN.cbl`, and treat the catalog as the source the API facade's documentation is generated from.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there are no API error-rate or latency metrics to alert on. Operational signalling consists of `NOTIFY=&SYSUID` on job completion (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 1) and `MSGCLASS=X` spool output. No CloudWatch alarms, anomaly detection, SLO alerting or paging integration exists, despite README noting the batch 'runs 5-7 hours and sometimes overruns' its window.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — API alerting is not applicable yet. Note that even the existing batch-overrun condition is unalerted, so degradation is discovered by downstream complaint.
findings.recommendation: Alert on batch duration against the window and on job abend now; add error-rate and latency alarms at the API facade when it is introduced.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false and has_auth_surface=false — the repository defines no agent-facing integration surface to govern. There is no IaC of any kind (searched for `*.tf`, CloudFormation templates, CDK entry points, Helm charts, Kustomize and Ansible: none found), no drift detection, and no review automation. The EC2 gateway, its network path and the `payroll` account exist only as hardcoded values in `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 15-21. README confirms 'No source control until the files were copied here in 2021'.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration. Nonetheless the infrastructure that will carry the agent integration (gateway, credentials, network path) is entirely manually managed, so the governance gap becomes material as soon as the API facade from API-Q1 is built.
findings.recommendation: Define the gateway, IAM/RACF roles, secrets and network path as code with peer-reviewed changes and drift detection before exposing any agent-facing endpoint.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there are no APIs to contract-test. There is also no CI/CD pipeline at all: searched for `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `buildspec.yml` and `appspec.yml` — none present. Compilation and promotion are manual, as implied by 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM' (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 5) and README's 'changes validated in a shared QA region only'.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — API contract testing is not applicable. The absence of any pipeline means there is also no automated gate for the fixed-width layout contract that consumers depend on (see DISC-Q1).
findings.recommendation: Stand up a pipeline that compiles, runs the ENG-Q4 tests, and diffs the published record layout for breaking changes; extend it to API contract tests once the facade exists.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there is no deployed request-serving surface to roll back. Deployment is a manual load-module replacement into `ACME.PAYROLL.LOADLIB` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 6); there is no blue/green config, no CodeDeploy rollback trigger, no feature flags and no traffic shifting. Data-side recovery is partially served by GDG generations (`PAYOUT(+1)`), which retain prior outputs but do not restore prior program versions.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration. Practically, reverting a bad payroll change depends on manual load-library restoration with no tested procedure, and GDG retention covers output files only.
findings.recommendation: Version load modules with a documented, tested restore procedure (and automate it in the ENG-Q2 pipeline) so a payroll-breaking change can be reverted predictably.

evaluations.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
evaluations.reason: No API/HTTP surface of any kind — no endpoints, no gateway, no throttling surface to document (searched for API Gateway usage plans, WAF rate rules and rate-limit headers: none, and no IaC exists). Informational absence suppressed per the scoring model; no finding emitted.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered: the system exposes no list/query endpoints (has_http_rpc_surface=false). Trigger condition is 'service has list/query endpoints with potentially unbounded results'.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: The system emits no metrics or telemetry of any kind — output is JES spool only (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl line 13); no put_metric_data, dashboards or KPI alarms exist. Informational absence suppressed per the scoring model; no finding emitted.

items.summary: Resolve the seven deployment blockers: build an API facade with machine identity, make the payout write path idempotent and reversible, scope sensitive fields, and establish an immutable audit trail and a residency-safe encrypted transfer.

Close agent-safety gaps: scoped and action-level authorization, credential management and revocation, concurrency and resilience controls, business blast-radius limits, approval/draft states, and PII redaction in diagnostics.

Raise agent effectiveness: async job semantics, queryable state and degradation signalling, versioned schema, input validation, temporal metadata, structured logging, automated tests, and encryption at rest.

recommended_actions.action: Build an API facade over the payroll batch system
recommended_actions.rationale: Every other control (identity, scoping, validation, rate limiting, tracing) attaches to a callable interface. Direct dataset access and nightly FTP cannot be made agent-safe.

recommended_actions.action: Establish machine identity and immutable audit attribution
recommended_actions.rationale: Identity precedes data access: without a distinct, revocable agent principal there is nothing to scope permissions against and no attributable trail for SOX-relevant payroll writes.

recommended_actions.action: Eliminate the hardcoded credential and plaintext PII transfer
recommended_actions.rationale: A 2003-era password is committed in jcl/PAYRUN.jcl and SSN plus bank account data crosses a trust boundary in cleartext — the highest-severity concrete exposure in the repository.

recommended_actions.action: Make the payout write path idempotent, reversible and bounded
recommended_actions.rationale: Agent retries and concurrency at machine speed against a non-idempotent, unbounded, non-reversible disbursement path is the dominant financial risk.

recommended_actions.action: Scope sensitive payroll fields out of consumer-facing data
recommended_actions.rationale: SSN and bank account travel with every record today; field scoping plus differentiated access is required before any agent reads payroll data.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce a proposed-run review gate before disbursement
recommended_actions.rationale: A staging-then-promote state gives both the human approval point and the reviewable intermediate state the system currently lacks entirely.

recommended_actions.action: Publish a versioned record schema and retire fixed-width coupling
recommended_actions.rationale: Consumers reverse-engineer byte offsets with no version marker; a published, versioned, semantically named schema is the prerequisite for reliable agent tool bindings.

recommended_actions.action: Stand up CI with tests, contract checks and observability
recommended_actions.rationale: There are zero automated tests, no pipeline and no structured logging, so agent-breaking changes and degraded output (missing state tax, stale tax tables) are undetectable.
